question.prompt: Driving along a highway, Megan noticed that her odometer showed \(15951\) (miles). This number is a palindrome—it reads the same forward and backward. Then \(2\) hours later, the odometer displayed the next higher palindrome. What was her average speed, in miles per hour, during this \(2\)-hour period?

solutions.title: Find the next palindrome
solutions.explanation:
In \(15951\), the palindrome condition forces the opening \(15\) to reappear backward as \(51\) after the middle digit \(9\). This lets us find the next reading without checking every intervening number.

The first three digits of \(15951\) form \(159\). Keeping these digits would force the same palindrome, so a larger palindrome needs a larger three-digit beginning. The smallest possibility is \(160\), which forces the final two digits to be \(61\). Thus the next palindrome is \(16061\). Any larger three-digit beginning would give a larger number.

The difference between the odometer readings is the distance Megan traveled:
\[
16061-15951=110\text{ miles}.
\]
Her average speed was therefore
\[
\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}=\frac{110}{2}=55\text{ miles per hour}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{55}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutions.title: Find the next palindrome from place value, then divide distance by time
